\documentclass{article}
\newcommand{\ii}{\mathrm{i}}
\title{A small many-body toolbox (synthetic test note)}
\begin{document}
\maketitle
Throughout $\beta>0$, $\Gamma>0$, $a>0$, $t>0$, real $\epsilon$, and $n_F(x)=1/(e^{\beta x}+1)$.
Partial fractions give
\begin{equation}\label{eq:pf}
\frac{1}{(x-a)(x-b)} = \frac{1}{a-b}\Bigl[\frac{1}{x-a}-\frac{1}{x-b}\Bigr].
\end{equation}
A telescoping residue sum is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:telescope}
\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{1}{(n+a)(n+a+1)} = \frac{1}{a+1}.
\end{equation}
The fermionic sum of three propagators with distinct real poles is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:triple}
\frac{1}{\beta}\sum_n \frac{1}{(\ii\omega_n-a)(\ii\omega_n-b)(\ii\omega_n-c)}
 = \frac{n_F(a)}{(a-b)(a-c)}+\frac{n_F(b)}{(b-a)(b-c)}+\frac{n_F(c)}{(c-a)(c-b)}.
\end{equation}
For small $x$ (near the chemical potential) the occupation expands as
\begin{equation}\label{eq:small}
n_F(x) = \frac12 - \frac{\beta x}{2} + \mathcal{O}(x^{3}),
\end{equation}
while a damped oscillation decays faster than any power,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:decay}
e^{-\Gamma t}\cos(\epsilon t) = \mathcal{O}(t^{-2}).
\end{equation}
The Lorentzian-weighted occupation is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:lorentz}
\int d\omega\,\frac{2\Gamma\, n_F(\omega)}{(\omega-\epsilon)^2+\Gamma^2}
 = \pi - 2\,\mathrm{Im}\,\psi\Bigl(\frac12+\frac{\beta(\Gamma+\ii\epsilon)}{2\pi}\Bigr),
\end{equation}
and its derivative with respect to the level position is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:trigamma}
\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{1}{(n+a)^2} = \psi'(a).
\end{equation}
Finally, the retarded propagator of a broadened level obeys
\begin{equation}\label{eq:spectral}
-2\,\mathrm{Im}\,\frac{1}{\omega-\epsilon+\ii\Gamma} = \frac{2\Gamma}{(\omega-\epsilon)^2+\Gamma^2}.
\end{equation}
\end{document}
